<p class="section-kicker">Why this course</p>
<h2>Build the evidence trail—not just the output.</h2>
<p>Accelerometers record acceleration, not ready-made measures of activity, sedentary behavior, or sleep. Credible results depend on the decisions made before, during, and after data collection.</p>
<p>This course connects those decisions into one practical workflow: define the protocol, preserve traceability, process raw files, interrogate data quality, and deliver a dataset another analyst can understand. Examples use ActiGraph, GGIR in R, and Stata, while the underlying principles extend beyond any one tool.</p>
:::

<p><span class="transcript-time">00:13</span> collecting accelerometer data is only the beginning. To turn a device recording into a trustworthy research dataset, every step has to be planned, documented, and checked. This course gives you a practical workflow for doing that work</p>
<p><span class="transcript-time">00:28</span> from start to finish. We begin with the core concepts. What does an accelerometer record? What kinds of outcomes can it support? Why do device placement and study protocol matter? Then we move into the hands-on workflow. Accelerometry</p>
<p><span class="transcript-time">00:44</span> turns raw movement into insight about how people move, rest, and sleep. Over eight modules, you&#x27;ll learn the complete workflow. Module 1 introduces the accelerometer—what it records, and how placement shapes the data. Module 2</p>

<p><span class="transcript-time">01:29</span> These tools help move the data from raw acceleration signals into interpretable summaries of physical activity, sedentary behavior, and sleep-wake patterns. Just as important, you will learn how to inspect data quality. A single summary</p>
<p><span class="transcript-time">01:45</span> number can hide problems, so the course emphasizes visual checks, clear decision rules, and careful notes about exclusions or concerns. By the end of the course, you should understand the complete path from planning and deploying</p>

::: {.section-wrap}
<p class="section-kicker">Choose your route</p>
<h2>Learn the logic, then decide how far to practise it.</h2>

::: {.workflow-grid .compact}
<div class="workflow-step"><span>3–4 hours</span><strong>Concept route</strong><p>Read the lessons, watch the videos or use their transcripts, and complete the self-checks. A web browser is sufficient.</p></div>
<div class="workflow-step"><span>6–9 hours</span><strong>Hands-on route</strong><p>Add every mini-activity and save the stated deliverables. Timing excludes software installation and full-dataset processing.</p></div>
:::

::: {.review-note}
<strong>Hands-on prerequisites:</strong> Bring an approved or fictional study protocol and a safe practice dataset with no direct identifiers. Modules 2–3 require access to a compatible ActiGraph device and ActiLife for the demonstrated workflow. Modules 4–6 use R, RStudio, and GGIR. Module 7 uses Stata. ActiLife and Stata access may depend on your laboratory or institution's licensing. Record the exact device, firmware, and software versions used in your own project.
:::
:::

::: {.workflow-section #audience}
::: {.section-wrap}
<p class="section-kicker">Who can use this course</p>
<h2>Built for learners and teams who work with movement data.</h2>
<p>The concept route is suitable for beginners with a web browser. The hands-on route is for learners who also have access to an approved or fictional protocol, safe practice data, and the demonstrated software or devices.</p>

::: {.workflow-grid}
<div class="workflow-step"><span>Study</span><strong>Undergraduate and graduate students</strong><p>Build a foundation in accelerometry for kinesiology, public health, epidemiology, data science, or related coursework and research.</p></div>
<div class="workflow-step"><span>Research operations</span><strong>Research assistants and study teams</strong><p>Use a shared workflow for device deployment, file traceability, quality review, and preparation of analysis-ready data.</p></div>
<div class="workflow-step"><span>Teaching and leadership</span><strong>Faculty, instructors, and investigators</strong><p>Support methods teaching, laboratory onboarding, protocol planning, and review of reproducible research practices.</p></div>
<div class="workflow-step"><span>Practice</span><strong>Health and movement professionals</strong><p>Understand how wearable data are collected and interpreted in public health, clinical, exercise, and human-movement settings.</p></div>
<div class="workflow-step"><span>Analysis</span><strong>Data analysts and methodologists</strong><p>Connect raw-device decisions with GGIR processing, quality-control evidence, documented cleaning, and final datasets.</p></div>
<div class="workflow-step"><span>Industry</span><strong>Company and consulting teams</strong><p>Develop shared literacy for work in wearable technology, digital health, occupational health, research services, and related fields.</p></div>
:::
:::

<section class="faq-section" id="faq" aria-labelledby="faq-heading">
<div class="section-wrap">
<p class="section-kicker">Questions before you begin</p>
<h2 id="faq-heading">Frequently asked questions</h2>
<p class="faq-intro">Find the practical details first, then review the decisions that must be adapted for your own study.</p>

<h3>Getting started</h3>
<div class="faq-grid">
<details class="faq-item" open>
<summary>Who is this course for?</summary>
<p>It is designed for undergraduate and graduate students; research assistants, coordinators, and laboratory teams; faculty, instructors, and investigators; public-health, clinical, exercise, and movement professionals; data analysts and methodologists; and company or consulting teams working in wearable technology, digital health, occupational health, or research services. The concept route is beginner-friendly, while the hands-on route requires appropriate software, devices, and safe practice data.</p>
</details>

<details class="faq-item">
<summary>How long does the course take?</summary>
<p>Allow about 3–4 hours for the concept route or 6–9 hours for the hands-on route. Full-dataset processing, software installation, and protocol approval take additional time. Each module card shows a planning estimate.</p>
</details>

<details class="faq-item">
<summary>Which devices and software does the course use?</summary>
<p>The examples use ActiGraph devices, ActiLife, GGIR in R, and Stata. You can complete the concept route in a browser. Hands-on work requires appropriate software and a safe practice dataset; access to ActiLife and Stata may depend on your laboratory or institution's licensing.</p>
</details>

<details class="faq-item">
<summary>Do I need previous experience with R, GGIR, or Stata?</summary>
<p>No prior experience is required for the concept route. For the hands-on route, you should be comfortable finding files, editing paths, running a script, reading software messages, and protecting participant data. Basic familiarity with R and Stata is helpful in Modules 4–7.</p>
</details>

<details class="faq-item">
<summary>How can I use the videos accessibly?</summary>
<p>Each video is followed by a quick summary, a full transcript, and a downloadable caption track. The summary is for rapid review; it is not a substitute for the transcript or captions. Software controls and visual-only details are described in the accompanying text where they affect the task.</p>
</details>

<details class="faq-item">
<summary>How do I know that I completed a module?</summary>
<p>Complete the self-check and compare your reasoning with the feedback. On the hands-on route, also save the module's stated deliverable—for example, a protocol decision, download log, GGIR configuration, QC log, or analysis script.</p>
</details>
</div>

<h3>Methods and files</h3>
<div class="faq-grid">
<details class="faq-item">
<summary>What does an accelerometer measure directly?</summary>
<p>It records acceleration over time, usually along three axes. Behaviors such as activity intensity, sedentary time, posture, and sleep are estimates derived from the raw signal using a documented algorithm, wear location, and protocol.</p>
</details>

<details class="faq-item">
<summary>Does GGIR require conversion from <code>.gt3x</code> to <code>.csv</code>?</summary>
<p>No. GGIR can read <code>.gt3x</code> files directly. Convert to CSV only when a downstream script, another software package, data-sharing requirement, or audit workflow specifically needs it.</p>
</details>

<details class="faq-item">
<summary>What is the difference between <code>.gt3x</code> and <code>.agd</code> files?</summary>
<p>A <code>.gt3x</code> file contains raw ActiGraph acceleration data. The demonstrated workflow also creates a 10-second <code>.agd</code>, a count-based epoch summary that may be useful for ActiLife review or legacy workflows. Follow the approved protocol if it specifies another epoch length.</p>
</details>

<details class="faq-item">
<summary>What counts as a valid participant record?</summary>
<p>The course example uses at least 4 valid days, at least 10 hours of awake wear per valid day, and at least 1 weekend day. These are example rules and must be approved for the study population, device, placement, and protocol.</p>
</details>

<details class="faq-item">
<summary>Are the course thresholds and cleaning rules universal?</summary>
<p>No. Device settings, valid-day rules, intensity thresholds, wear criteria, and variable-specific cleaning rules are study-specific examples. Confirm every rule against the approved protocol, the exact software version, and the relevant output dictionary before applying it.</p>
</details>

<details class="faq-item">
<summary>What should the final analysis package contain?</summary>
<p>Include a dated <code>.dta</code> file, data dictionary, cleaning log, exclusion table, Stata do-file, and a README that identifies the source GGIR run and processing batches.</p>
</details>
</div>
</div>
